content.title: About
content.content: Bologna is a cooked‑smoked sausage made from beef and pork, seasoned with spices and flavorings. In the reduced‑sodium version the salt content is cut to 0.5 g per 100 g, making it more suitable for people watching their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Although called “Italian sausage,” the modern bologna originated in the United States in the early 20th century.
Sodium reduction is achieved by replacing part of the salt with potassium chloride and using natural flavor enhancers.
Bologna is commonly used in sandwiches, salads, and as an ingredient in hot dishes such as pasta.
The classic recipe blends beef, pork, and sometimes veal, giving it a distinctive flavor.
Reduced‑sodium bologna can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks after opening.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 15 g of high‑quality animal protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron supports normal hemoglobin levels and energy metabolism.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps control blood pressure and lessens strain on the cardiovascular system.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Bologna supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef or pork.

items.title: Nitrite content
items.content: Like most smoked sausages, bologna can contain nitrites, which are undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Despite lower sodium, the product remains relatively fatty; portion control is advised for those monitoring fat intake.

items.title: Potassium level
items.content: People with kidney disease should watch potassium chloride intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice bologna thinly for sandwiches, add it to salads, use it in hot dishes (pasta, casseroles) or grill it. Let the slices reach room temperature before serving to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bologna in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at +4 °C. After opening, consume within 7‑10 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

chicken-drumstick-fried-coated-skin-coat.title: Chicken drumstick, fried, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken drumstick deep‑fried in a crispy coating is a staple of fast‑food and restaurant menus. Both the skin and the coating are edible, giving the piece a golden color, aromatic flavor, and crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Deep‑frying is typically done at 175‑190 °C, creating a fast‑forming golden crust.
The coating often contains a blend of flour, spices, and sometimes breadcrumbs, enhancing taste and aroma.
Drumsticks have more connective tissue than breast meat, which helps them stay juicy after frying.
In the United States, breaded fried drumsticks are among the top‑selling items in major fast‑food chains.
They are commonly served with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, spicy chili, and others.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken meat provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Drumsticks are a source of phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Iron
items.content: While lower than red meat, chicken still contributes to maintaining healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat in the coating helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying and coating increase the dish’s calories and saturated fat levels.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Repeated use of frying oil can generate trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Coatings are often salted; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The breading may contain gluten, dairy, or nuts, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Acrylamide
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried drumsticks are usually eaten by hand, dipped in a sauce. They can also be added to salads, placed in a sandwich, or served alongside fries, rice, or vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked drumsticks in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days in an airtight container. For longer storage, freeze them for up to 2 months. Reheat in an oven or air‑fryer to restore crispness.

infant-formula-enfamil-ar-powder-made-wi.title: Infant formula, Enfamil AR, powder, made with water

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil AR is a powdered infant formula designed for children with higher energy and nutrient needs. It provides proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and added DHA and ARA to support brain and eye development. The powder is reconstituted with water to create a ready‑to‑feed product.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Enfamil AR is formulated for infants with rapid growth and weight gain.
Contains easily digestible whey‑based protein.
Includes prebiotics to support a healthy gut microbiome.
Clinically tested for safety and efficacy.
Packaging is designed for convenient dosing during preparation.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: A balanced mix of macro‑ and micronutrients meets the needs of a growing body.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA aid in the formation of neural cells and visual system.

items.title: Gut health
items.content: Prebiotics promote beneficial bacteria, improving digestion.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc help maintain the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Higher fat and carbohydrate content supplies extra energy for active infants.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Children with known cow‑milk allergy may react to the formula.

items.title: Improper reconstitution
items.content: Too concentrated or too diluted mixtures can lead to dehydration or overfeeding.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Excessive intake may contribute to dental caries.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Powder can absorb moisture, degrading quality and fostering microbial growth.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix the powder with clean, boiled water cooled to body temperature (≈37 °C). Follow the label’s instructions for the amount of powder per volume of water. Consume the prepared formula within 2 hours.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened container in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the bag tightly sealed and use within 30 days.

pasta-whole-grain-with-tomato-based-sauc.title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Seafood

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato sauce and seafood is a dish that combines whole‑grain pasta, a flavorful tomato‑based sauce, and a variety of seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari). Whole grain pasta retains more fiber and nutrients than refined white pasta, while the tomato sauce provides lycopene and vitamin C. Seafood adds high‑quality protein, omega‑3 fatty acids, and essential minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains roughly twice the fiber of regular refined pasta.
Tomatoes used in the sauce are rich in lycopene, which becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Seafood such as mussels and shrimp are natural sources of vitamin B12, rare in plant foods.
The tradition of pairing pasta with seafood originates from Mediterranean cuisine, where both are staples.
Cooking whole grain pasta takes slightly longer, but it holds a firmer texture.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and blood‑sugar regulation.

items.title: Protein and omega‑3 source
items.content: Seafood contributes complete protein and omega‑3 fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Lycopene and vitamin C
items.content: The tomato sauce supplies antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Seafood adds zinc, iron, and selenium, important for immune function and metabolism.

items.title: Lower glycemic index
items.content: Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index than white pasta, aiding appetite control.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or calamari.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Food contaminants
items.content: Certain seafood can contain heavy metals; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Overeating
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑dense due to pasta and oil in the sauce; keep portions moderate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pasta al dente, then toss it with hot tomato sauce and sautéed seafood. Garnish with fresh parsley, basil, or grated Parmesan. Serve immediately while the sauce is warm.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep unused seafood separate, chilled, and consume within 24 hours. Dry whole grain pasta should be kept in a cool, dry place.

pastry-chinese-made-with-rice-flour.title: Pastry, Chinese, made with rice flour

content.title: About
content.content: Chinese rice‑flour pastry is a traditional dessert made from a thin dough of rice flour, often filled with sweet red bean, sesame paste, or fruit. The dough is soft and slightly sticky, giving the finished pastry a delicate rice aroma and gentle sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice‑flour dough makes the pastry gluten‑free, important for people with celiac disease.
In China these pastries are commonly served during tea ceremonies as a light sweet between dishes.
Traditionally they are steamed, but modern versions can be baked for a crispier crust.
Fillings range from sweet red bean to fragrant lotus seed paste.
Baking with rice flour creates a slightly crunchy outer layer.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Rice flour contains no gluten, making the pastry safe for those with gluten intolerance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with wheat‑based baked goods, these pastries usually contain less saturated fat.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice flour provides slow‑releasing carbohydrates that help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice flour supplies thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The pastry offers magnesium and phosphorus, beneficial for muscle and bone health.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may be allergic to rice flour.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice flour can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium in fillings
items.content: Certain fillings (e.g., soy‑based sauces) may add extra sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The pastry can be enjoyed on its own, served with tea, or used as a base for fruit salads. Cut into bite‑size pieces and pair with berries or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the pastries in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C; reheat by steaming or microwaving before serving.
